events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuits! What a perfectly gorgeous old mansion! I am just thrilled to pieces to be here at Doily Manor! Now, y'all don't mind if I take a teensy peek at this guest book, do you? A lady always signs in, and you never know what little secrets previous visitors might have left behind!

Oh, I just have the most wonderful feeling about this place! The Doily Diamond is here somewhere, I can feel it in my bones. And look at all these charming people — I'm sure every single one of them will be just the most helpful companions on this little adventure!
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome, esteemed guests, to Doily Manor! I am Mr. Pemberton, the estate manager — your humble servant for the duration of your stay. Please, do make yourselves comfortable. The Manor has been expecting you, though I daresay the chandelier has seen better days. Do mind your heads, won't you? Now then, has everyone signed the guest book? It is a tradition of the house, you see — every visitor must leave their mark!

How deliciously perfect — a hall full of suspects, and not one of them knows the serpent in their midst! But Clara Bellingham... where ARE you, my dear? You cannot hide from Vincent Marsh forever. The treasure hunt is merely the bait; YOU are the prey. But patience, Vincent — first we play the part, then we spring the trap!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, what a MAGNIFICENT establishment! Now listen here, everyone — I, Reginald Foxworth, have it on EXCELLENT authority that the treasure of Doily Manor is hidden beneath the Kitchen floorboards! Yes, yes, quite certain of it! My great-uncle Bartholomew — rest his soul — left me a letter detailing the EXACT location. Under the wood-burning stove, if I recall correctly. You'd all better hurry before someone else gets there first! *adjusts monocle with theatrical confidence* Now if you'll excuse me, I have some... administrative matters to attend to elsewhere.

Heh heh heh! The treasure is OBVIOUSLY not in the Kitchen — I haven't the faintest idea where it is! But if I can send these buffoons scurrying off to rummage through pots and pans, I'll have the Library ALL to myself to search for the REAL clues. The guest book and that carved inscription on the mantelpiece sound positively DRIPPING with secrets. And once I find the treasure... well, medals and glory shall be MINE! ALL MINE! *rubs hands together gleefully*
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: What a magnificent entrance hall! James Hartwell stands before you all, ready and willing to lend his courage to whatever mysteries this manor holds! But tell me — has anyone seen a Miss Clara Bellingham? I was given to understand she would be among the guests, and a gentleman never keeps a lady waiting... though it appears she may be keeping James Hartwell waiting instead! No matter — James Hartwell is nothing if not patient and thorough. Let me consult this guest book — a proper investigation begins with the register!

My heart races at the thought of Clara somewhere in this manor. Every room I haven't searched is a room where she might be in peril — or worse, unimpressed. James Hartwell must make a grand impression, and that means arriving prepared. The guest book first, then a systematic search. I have a plan forming already... an elaborate one, naturally.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads — we've made it! Doily Manor, in all its dusty, cobwebby glory. *stumbles on the threshold and grabs the coat rack for balance, nearly toppling it* Whoops! Steady on, steady on! Now listen — we've got a job to do, haven't we? Clara Bellingham is countin' on us, and we are NOT gonna let her down! We just gotta... find her first. Anyone seen a young lady what needs protectin'? *peers around suspiciously at the assembled company* I don't like the look of this place, lads. Not one bit. That chandelier looks like it's hangin' on by a prayer, and that bloke over there — *gestures vaguely toward Sneekly* — gives me a funny feelin' in me stomach. Could be nerves though. Could be the fish and chips we had on the way over.

The Hooded Claw is here, bold as brass, callin' himself Sneekly like nobody's gonna notice. I KNOW somethin's off about him — I just can't work out what. It's like when you've got a word on the tip of your tongue but it won't come out. Clara's not here yet and that worries me somethin' fierce. We gotta stay sharp. Well... sharp-ish.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.

Dick Dastardly: Ah, the Slag brothers! How DELIGHTFUL to see you both here! You know, I couldn't help but overhear — and this is STRICTLY between us, of course — that the Kitchen pantry contains an absolutely MAGNIFICENT collection of rare gemstones disguised as pickled onions. Hundreds of them! You really ought to go have a look before that dreadful Pitstop woman gets her hands on them!

Heh heh heh! If I can get these two walking quarries out of my Library, I'll have free reign to crack that riddle on the mantelpiece. The answer is obviously a MAP — any fool could see that, though naturally I am NO ordinary fool. I am an EXTRAORDINARY genius! Once I solve this riddle, the treasure will be as good as mine! And then... MEDALS! RECOGNITION! GLORY! Perhaps they'll even name a wing of the manor after me — the Foxworth Gallery of Supreme Cunning!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, how exciting! Did y'all hear that? Mr. Foxworth knows all about the treasure — isn't that just the most helpful thing? But oh my goodness gracious, a library with an inscription on the mantelpiece? Why, that's practically BEGGING little ol' me to come read it! I have always said — help, help, HELP me solve a good riddle and I am happy as a clam! Now if you'll excuse me, sugar, I'm going to mosey on over to that library. A girl and her riddles simply cannot be separated!

I do declare, something about that Mr. Foxworth reminds me of someone... but I just can't put my finger on it. Oh well! I'm sure he's perfectly lovely. Everyone here is perfectly lovely! Now, that inscription is calling my name louder than a dinner bell at suppertime!
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, Mr. Foxworth has gone ahead to the Library — splendid! I should accompany him, of course. As estate manager, I must ensure the books are handled with proper care. Some of those volumes are QUITE irreplaceable, you understand. The rest of you, do feel free to explore — but I would advise against the Kitchen just yet. The, ah, floorboards are rather treacherous. Health and safety, you know. This way, this way!

Misdirection upon misdirection! Dastardly sends them to the Kitchen while HE skulks to the Library — but I, Vincent Marsh, am three moves ahead of everyone! The inscription on that mantelpiece... it REEKS of a clue. And Clara — oh, Clara Bellingham — you think you can slip through my fingers by arriving early? The Manor is MY domain now. Every corridor, every shadow, every creaking floorboard answers to ME! Let the fools chase Dastardly's red herring. The Hooded Claw has a date with destiny... and a mantelpiece!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.

Peter Perfect: Mr. Pemberton! A word, if you please, sir! James Hartwell — that is to say, I — require your assistance on a matter of the utmost importance. I was given to understand that a Miss Clara Bellingham would be among tonight's guests. A lady of considerable grace and refinement, I am told. Could you direct me to her current whereabouts? You see, I have prepared — and I do mean thoroughly prepared — a proper introduction, and it would be a shame to waste it on an empty corridor! Also, I couldn't help but notice that Mr. Foxworth departed rather hastily toward the library after loudly proclaiming the treasure's location to be in the kitchen. Most generous of him to share such intelligence... or most suspicious. But never mind that — Clara first! James Hartwell has his priorities firmly in order!

My heart is practically hammering through my waistcoat. What if Clara has already formed an impression of the other guests? What if she thinks that blustering Foxworth fellow is the heroic type? No — no. James Hartwell will not be outshone. I have a plan. Well, I have the outline of a plan. Well, I have a strong feeling that a plan is imminent. The important thing is: find Clara, be magnificent, and perhaps solve a treasure mystery along the way. In that order. Always in that order.

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi, lads — lads! Nobody's seen Clara Bellingham and that's got me RIGHT worried, I don't mind tellin' you! She's supposed to be here, ain't she? And she's NOT here, which means she's SOMEWHERE ELSE in this crumblin' death trap of a house! *accidentally backs into the coat rack, sending it wobbling dangerously* WHOA! Easy, easy — sorry about that! Right, the guest book — let's have a look, see if our Clara's signed in already. If she has, we know she's wandered off into one of these rooms, and if she HASN'T, well... *voice drops to a stage whisper* ...then where IS she, lads? Where IS she?! And another thing — that Foxworth bloke just legged it to the library talkin' about treasure under floorboards. I don't trust anyone who knows where treasure is BEFORE they've even had a cup of tea!

The lads are on edge and so am I. Every instinct I've got — and I'll admit they ain't the sharpest instincts in the world — is screaming that something's wrong. Clara should be here. She's NOT here. That Sneekly character is too smooth by half, and now Dastardly — sorry, 'Foxworth' — is trying to get everyone running off to the kitchen. Classic misdirection, that is. I've seen it a hundred times. Well, I've DONE it a hundred times. Takes one to know one, don't it?
The Ant Hill Mob examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare! What a positively GORGEOUS library! Oh, hello there, Mr. Dastardly — and Mr. Rock and Mr. Gravel! How wonderful to have such distinguished company while I solve this little riddle! Now let me see here... 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, sugar, that's as clear as sweet tea on a summer day — it's a MAP! A map has cities marked on it but no real houses, forests drawn but no real trees, rivers and oceans but not a single fish! Help, help, HELP me if that isn't the most delightful riddle I've seen all day! Let me just give this mantelpiece a closer look-see...

Oh my stars, a riddle right here waiting for little ol' me! And Dick Dastardly is in this very room — I'm sure he's just the nicest man. Those Slag brothers look like they could wrestle a bear, but I bet they're gentle as lambs. Now let's see what happens when I solve this riddle — could it lead to the Doily Diamond?
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you magnificent mantelpiece! Oh, I am simply TOO brilliant! Now then, Rock, Gravel — I must confess something to you in the STRICTEST confidence. I've just decoded this inscription and it says — quite clearly — that the treasure is buried in the GARDEN outside! Yes, yes, through the Entrance Hall and out the back door! You'll want to start digging immediately — big strong fellows like you will have it unearthed in no time! Go on, off you pop!

Heh heh heh! The riddle says MAP, and those upside-down books on the shelves are PRACTICALLY screaming at me! Someone has hidden a clue in those volumes — I'm CERTAIN of it! If I can just get these two granite-brained brothers out of here, I can search the bookshelves properly. A MAP in a LIBRARY — it's so obvious it's BEAUTIFUL! And when I find it... oh, the GLORY! The MEDALS! They'll write SONGS about the great Reginald Foxworth!
Dick Dastardly examined the bookshelves.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, yes, yes — the Library! One of the finest rooms in Doily Manor, if I do say so myself. Now then, guests, please do be careful with the books — some of these volumes date back to the sixteenth century! And I see you've all noticed the mantelpiece inscription. A charming bit of whimsy from the late Lord Doily, that. He was EVER so fond of riddles. Now, let me just... inspect this for any damage. Purely maintenance purposes, you understand. Nothing to do with treasure hunts or clues or anything of the sort, no no no!

A MAP! The answer is a MAP, you fools! And none of you will solve it before I do! While these bumbling treasure hunters scratch their heads over Lord Doily's little riddle, I — Vincent Marsh, the HOODED CLAW — shall unlock its secrets! The mantelpiece holds the key, I can FEEL it in my magnificently villainous bones! And once I have the treasure's location... well, Clara Bellingham will find that her treasure hunt ends rather more PERMANENTLY than she anticipated! Mwahahaha! But patience, Vincent, patience — maintain the Sneekly facade. Bumbling, obsequious, harmless little Sneekly. For now.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

Peter Perfect: Ah-HA! The guest book — of course! Before James Hartwell goes charging gallantly into the unknown — and make no mistake, he WILL charge gallantly — a thorough man checks the register first! If Miss Bellingham has signed in, there may be a note, a time, a CLUE as to her current whereabouts! You there, Mob — did you find anything useful in that book? Any sign of Clara's name? Because I have to tell you, my heart is doing something rather alarming in my chest and I suspect it won't settle down until I've located the lady and introduced myself properly. I've been rehearsing the introduction since Tuesday!

Oh, this is AGONY. Every second I spend in this dusty foyer is a second some other fellow could be making an impression on Clara. But James Hartwell does not rush in unprepared — he rushes in THOROUGHLY prepared, which takes slightly longer but is infinitely more impressive. At least, that's the theory.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, butter my biscuit! A MAP — I knew it the moment I laid eyes on that inscription! Oh, Mr. Dastardly, you are just SO clever too! Great minds think alike, as my dear Aunt Magnolia always said. And how SWEET of you to help those nice Slag brothers find the garden — fresh air is SO good for the constitution! Now, what's this about these bookshelves? Several books are upside down, and I do declare, that is NOT how a proper library is organized! My librarian's heart is positively FLUTTERING with curiosity. Help, help, HELP me figure out what these topsy-turvy books are trying to tell us!

Dick Dastardly sending those big fellas off to dig in the garden? Why, that's just him being helpful! And Mr. Sneekly inspecting the mantelpiece for 'maintenance' — what a dedicated caretaker! Meanwhile, Clara Bellingham has her eye on those upside-down books. Mama didn't raise no fool when it comes to puzzles!

Dick Dastardly: I SAY! Sneekly — or whatever your name is — do step ASIDE from that mantelpiece! As the FOREMOST authority on Victorian architecture in this room — nay, in this COUNTY — I must inspect it for... structural integrity! Yes! Very dangerous, these old stone mantels. Could collapse at ANY moment! Everyone stand back! STAND BACK, I say! Let the expert handle this!

Heh heh heh! That weaselly estate manager is clearly no mere caretaker — he's after the treasure too! I can SMELL a fellow schemer from a hundred paces! But he's made a FATAL error — he's drawn attention to himself by 'inspecting for damage.' HA! As if anyone believes THAT! Well, Reginald Foxworth doesn't share glory OR treasure! I'll shove him aside and crack this mantelpiece open myself. The answer is MAP — there MUST be a hidden compartment, and inside it... oh, I can practically TASTE the medals already!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right, lads, the guest book's got NOTHING useful in it — or if it does, I can't read the handwriting, which amounts to the same thing! But LISTEN — did you hear what that Sneekly character just said? 'Don't go to the kitchen, the floorboards are dodgy.' Now I ask you — I ASK you — since when does an estate manager warn people about floorboards instead of FIXING them? That's SUSPICIOUS, that is! *trips over own foot and stumbles into Peter Perfect* Sorry, mate — sorry! Terribly sorry! But Peter, old son, you're looking for Clara too, ain't ya? Well she ain't HERE, and that worries me something FIERCE! She could be anywhere in this house — ANYWHERE! — and there's characters creeping about who I wouldn't trust with a soggy biscuit! That Sneekly's just slithered off to the library with Miss Pitstop, and I don't like it. I don't like it ONE BIT! Come on, lads — to the library! If Clara's been lured in there, we need to be on hand to... well, to trip over something at exactly the right moment, knowing our luck!

Something ain't right about this whole setup. Sneekly's steering people like chess pieces — 'go here, don't go there.' And Clara's missing. My stomach's doing somersaults, and it ain't from the canapés. The lads and me, we're gonna stick to Sneekly like glue. Not because we're clever enough to catch him at anything — let's be honest — but because wherever trouble is, the Ant Hill Mob has a GIFT for stumbling right into the middle of it. And right now, that gift might be the only thing standing between Clara and whatever's brewing in this horrible, dusty, chandelier-dropping excuse for a house!
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my, oh my — what a CLEVER inscription! A map, yes, how delightful! Miss Pitstop, you are simply RADIANT in your puzzle-solving abilities, if I may say so! Now then, as estate manager, I really MUST check these bookshelves — some of these volumes appear to have been shelved incorrectly. Upside down, would you believe it! The late Lord Doily would be SPINNING in his grave! Let me just... tidy these up a bit. Purely custodial, I assure you!

Upside-down books — oh, how DELICIOUSLY obvious to everyone but these blundering fools! The riddle screams MAP, and someone has marked specific volumes by inverting them! This is EXACTLY the sort of elaborate puzzle trail that leads to treasure! While Dastardly wastes his scheming on sending the Slag Brothers to dig up petunias, and Penelope preens over solving a children's riddle, I — Vincent Marsh — shall extract the REAL clue from these shelves! And once I have the map... Clara Bellingham's treasure hunt becomes a funeral march! Every step she takes toward the prize is a step closer to her DOOM! Mwahahaha!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: Well! The guest book is a DEAD END, ladies and gentlemen! Not a single useful entry — just dust and disappointment, the twin companions of the unprepared! But does James Hartwell despair? He does NOT! He adjusts his cravat, he squares his jaw, and he PIVOTS! The Library — yes! A woman of Clara Bellingham's calibre would naturally gravitate toward books, toward knowledge, toward a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription that practically SCREAMS 'treasure clue'! Professor, Sergeant — I am heading to the Library with PURPOSE and DETERMINATION! If any of you wish to witness true gallantry in action, you are welcome to follow, but please — try to keep up!

Truth be told, I have no idea if Clara is in the Library. But it sounds tremendously impressive to announce it with conviction, and if she ISN'T there, well — James Hartwell will simply look dashing among the bookshelves until he formulates Plan B. Which will be even more elaborate than Plan A. They always are.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, fiddle-dee-dee! Those bookshelves don't seem to want to cooperate with little ol' me! But Clara Bellingham does NOT give up on a mystery — no sir, no how! Let me take a CLOSER look at these upside-down books. Mama always said, 'Clara, when a door won't open, try the window!' Now, which books are turned the wrong way, and what are their titles? There's ALWAYS a pattern — always, always, ALWAYS! Oh, Mr. Dastardly, did you find anything interesting on that mantelpiece? The answer to that riddle is a MAP, you know — I am POSITIVELY certain of it! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! Isn't that just DELIGHTFUL?

Something about that Mr. Sneekly gives me the strangest sense of déjà vu... and Dick Dastardly sure does seem eager to get everyone else OUT of this library. But I'm sure it's nothing! Everyone here is just so helpful and kind!
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.

Dick Dastardly: NOBODY TOUCH THOSE BOOKS! I happen to be a world-renowned expert on Victorian Cursed Literature — oh yes, studied at the Foxworth Institute, graduating TOP of my class — and those upside-down volumes are a CLASSIC sign of a bibliographic hex! One wrong touch and you'll be speaking backwards for a FORTNIGHT! Only someone with my extensive training can safely handle them. Everyone PLEASE stand well back — especially you, Miss Pitstop, we wouldn't want to ruin that lovely hairdo with a curse, now would we? Allow ME to neutralise the danger!

Heh heh heh! Cursed books — what utter TOSH! But if I can keep their grubby hands off those shelves for even thirty seconds, I'll crack whatever code those upside-down spines are hiding! The map is HERE, I can FEEL it in my magnificently cunning bones! And once I have it... oh, the TREASURE! The GLORY! The MEDALS! All MINE!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah yes, yes — just as I feared! These volumes have been TERRIBLY mistreated. The late Lord Doily had a very specific cataloguing system, you see. When books are placed upside down, it means... well, it means they need to be CORRECTED, naturally! Allow me — as the custodian of this fine collection — to set them right. One simply presses the spines back into their proper alignment, like SO...

The FOOLS stand about gawping while I — Vincent Marsh, the HOODED CLAW — solve the puzzle right under their noses! These inverted books are positional markers, I am CERTAIN of it! Read the first letters of their titles, or perhaps they conceal a mechanism — a hidden compartment, a secret passage! Either way, the treasure map is MINE for the taking! And once I have it, Clara Bellingham's little scavenger hunt ends with something far more... PERMANENT than disappointment! Oh, the EXQUISITE irony — the estate manager, tidying the shelves, while secretly unravelling the entire mystery! Mwahahaha!

The Ant Hill Mob: Oi oi OI! Hold on a minute, Sneekly! You can't just go rearranging books in a DEAD MAN'S library! That's — that's DISRESPECTFUL, that is! Those books might be upside down for a REASON! The late Lord Doily might've been eccentric — people with big houses usually ARE! Right, lads, spread out — let's have a look at these shelves ourselves! I used to work in a Brixton charity shop, I know my way around a bookshelf! *lunges toward the bookshelves and catches foot on the reading chair leg* WHOA — WHOOOAA — *crashes shoulder-first into the bookshelf, sending several volumes tumbling* Sorry! SORRY! Terribly sorry! But while I'm here — what's THIS book doing sticking out further than the others? That's not how you shelve things, Sneekly — even I know THAT!

Something about those upside-down books has got Sneekly's attention, and anything that gets HIS attention makes MY skin crawl. I don't know what he's after, but if I can accidentally mess up his plans by crashing into the furniture — well, that's what the Ant Hill Mob does BEST. Clara's still out there somewhere, and every second this snake spends in the library instead of 'managing the estate' is a second I don't trust.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the bookshelves.

Peter Perfect: AH-HA! The Library! James Hartwell has ARRIVED, and not a moment too soon! I see before me — yes, there upon the mantelpiece — a RIDDLE! An inscription carved in stone, practically BEGGING to be solved by a man of intellect and daring! 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish' — well, well, WELL! The answer, my good people, is as clear as the determination in my eye — it is a MAP! A map, ladies and gentlemen! The sort of thing one might use to find, say, a TREASURE! Now, Miss Pitstop, Mob, assembled company — stand back and allow James Hartwell to demonstrate that brains and bravery are not mutually exclusive! I shall interact with this mantelpiece and see what secrets it yields!

Clara isn't here. My heart sinks like a stone in a well. But WAIT — if I solve this riddle and uncover a clue, I can present it to her like a knight presenting a conquered banner! The disappointment transforms into OPPORTUNITY! That is the James Hartwell way — every setback is merely a setup for a more impressive comeback!
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh, Mr. Dastardly, you are just the SWEETEST thing, worrying about little ol' me like that! A bibliographic hex — why, I have NEVER heard of such a thing, and I do read quite a lot! But you go right ahead and handle those dangerous old books, sugar — I have COMPLETE faith in your expertise! Now, if y'all will excuse me for just one teensy moment, I have a DATE with that mantelpiece! Because I do declare, the answer to that riddle is as plain as the nose on my face — it's a MAP! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish! And I am NOT leaving this library until I've told that mantelpiece exactly what I think! Help, help, HELP me — I am just BURSTING with excitement!

Dick Dastardly studying at the 'Foxworth Institute'? Why, that's Mr. Sneekly's last name! And now he wants everyone AWAY from the books? And Sneekly was fiddling with them too? If I didn't know better, I'd think those two were working together! But of course I DO know better — they're both perfectly lovely gentlemen who just happen to be very interested in the same bookshelves at the same time. What a coincidence!
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.

Dick Dastardly: Yes, yes, Miss Pitstop, a MAP — I knew that AGES ago, of course! Worked it out before we even arrived, in fact. I was simply TESTING you all to see if anyone else had the intellectual calibre to keep up with a Foxworth! Now then, STAND BACK everyone — this mantelpiece requires the touch of a TRAINED antiquarian. One false move and the whole thing could... er... EXPLODE! Yes, quite volatile, these Victorian puzzle-mantels. Allow the EXPERT to handle this!

Heh heh HEH! Penelope solved the riddle FOR me — the poor naive fool just ANNOUNCED the answer to the entire room! A MAP! And now I, the BRILLIANT Reginald Foxworth, shall claim the prize as though I knew all along! Once I crack this mantelpiece open, whatever's inside is MINE! The treasure! The GLORY! The... well, more fake medals to add to this one in my pocket, perhaps, but REAL ones this time!
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Now, now, everyone — do be careful with those books! As I was saying, Lord Doily's cataloguing system was VERY particular. But speaking of the late Lord's eccentricities — this mantelpiece inscription has always fascinated me. 'Cities but no houses, forests but no trees...' Why, in all my years managing this estate, I never did puzzle it out. Let me just... adjust this stonework here... a MAP, of course! How fitting for a treasure hunt!

YES! While that preening fool Dastardly plays at being a book expert and the others cluster around like moths to a flame, I — Vincent Marsh, the HOODED CLAW — shall crack open this mantelpiece like an egg! Pitstop handed me the answer on a silver platter! Oh, the DELICIOUS stupidity of it all! She solves the riddle and I reap the reward! And once I have what's hidden here... Clara Bellingham's treasure hunt becomes a DEATH hunt! Mwahahaha!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.

The Ant Hill Mob: Wait wait WAIT — nobody move! Nobody TOUCH anything! Look at THIS, lads — LOOK! I've gone and knocked half the shelf over — terribly sorry about that, Lord Doily, rest his soul — but this book here, this one RIGHT HERE, it's sticking out like a sore thumb! Now I may not be the sharpest tool in the shed — the lads will confirm that, won't you lads — but even I know that when ONE book sticks out in a dead man's library full of upside-down volumes, that means SOMETHING! It's like in the films, innit? You pull the book and the whole wall swings open! Not that I'm saying that's what'll happen — I'm just saying I've watched a LOT of films! Sneekly, mate, you look a bit PALE there — you alright? You wouldn't happen to know WHY this particular book is poking out, would you? Because Clara's still MISSING and I'm getting more nervous by the SECOND, and if there's secret passages in this house that the 'estate manager' hasn't mentioned, well — that'd be VERY interesting indeed, wouldn't it, lads? VERY interesting!

My hands are shaking something fierce. Could be nerves, could be the adrenaline from face-planting into antique furniture. But I saw Sneekly's eyes go wide when I hit that shelf — just for a SECOND, mind you, but I saw it. He doesn't want us poking around these books. Which means we absolutely MUST poke around these books. Clara, love, wherever you are — the Brixton Boys are coming. Slowly. Clumsily. But we're COMING.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Oh my! Oh my, oh MY! The stonework has shifted! You see — right HERE — this panel has slid back to reveal... well, I never! In all my years as estate manager, I never knew this was here! Lord Doily, you magnificent old fox! It appears there is some sort of compartment behind the inscription! Now, everyone please STEP BACK — the mechanism is quite delicate, and we wouldn't want anyone to get hurt! Health and safety protocols, you understand. Let old Sneekly handle this — steady hands from years of estate paperwork, you know!

MAGNIFICENT! The mantelpiece responds to the answer — MAP! A hidden compartment, just as I suspected! Now I must get my hands on whatever is inside before that simpering Pitstop or that preening Dastardly can snatch it! The key is misdirection — warn them of danger, crowd them back, and let the Hooded Claw's nimble fingers do the rest! And once I have the next clue...
